The seal the channel last wrote on a row, from the log

log_channel_seal.Rd

The value of the round's last execution, log_executions(), in the row's current life: the seal of the version the round last carried out. What the round compares the row against to tell whether it changed since, with the channel's account configured (decided on 2026-10-17), in place of the applied_seal field. The field is @READONLY on the form and written by an import as any other: a referent who changes a row and imports the seal of the changed row, a public hash, would make it look untouched, and the change would be carried out on the owner's rights. The log names who wrote each seal, as it names who wrote each owner.

Usage

log_channel_seal(events, record, channel_account)

Arguments

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id to look at.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more. Not NULL: without them the round reads the field.

Value

One seal; "" when the channel never sealed the row in its current life, which makes it a row never carried out.
